CHEMISTRY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. newton (N)
   D. watt (W)

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

4. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Producers
   D. Decomposers only

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.

7. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

8. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.

10. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 37 °C

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain The Mole and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
